story.title: Cinderella
story.description: Mistreated by her stepmother and stepsisters, a young woman finds a chance to change her fate in a single night at a ball.
story.author: Charles Perrault

chapters.name: A Servant in Her Own House
chapters.summary: Cinderella's place in her father's house once her stepmother takes charge, and the royal invitation that finally gives her something to lose.

chapters.name: One Night at the Palace
chapters.summary: The Fairy Godmother lends rather than gives. Everything Cinderella gains that night is borrowed against a deadline she agrees to in advance.

chapters.name: The Slipper's Search
chapters.summary: The one thing the spell fails to take back travels the kingdom house by house, until the household that hid her has to answer the door.

scenes.name: A servant's life
scenes.summary: Cinderella sleeps by the kitchen fire and answers to her stepmother and both stepsisters. The ashes that give her her name are the first thing anyone notices about her, and by now the only thing.

scenes.name: The invitation to the ball
scenes.summary: A royal invitation arrives for a ball where the prince will choose a bride. It is addressed to every young woman in the kingdom, which is precisely the problem: Cinderella is one of them, and everyone in the house knows it.

scenes.name: The torn dress
scenes.summary: The stepsisters pull apart the dress Cinderella made from what she was allowed to keep, and the stepmother calls the matter settled. Nobody forbids her to go. They simply arrange for it to be impossible.

scenes.name: The Fairy Godmother
scenes.summary: Left crying in the garden, Cinderella is answered. The Fairy Godmother asks for a pumpkin, six mice and a pair of lizards, and names a condition instead of a price.

scenes.name: The pumpkin and the mice
scenes.summary: The garden empties itself into a carriage, a team of horses and a coachman, and Cinderella's rags become a gown. Only the glass slippers are made from nothing that was there before.

scenes.name: The stranger at the ball
scenes.summary: Nobody at the palace recognises her, her own family least of all. The prince dances with her the whole evening and never once asks her name - an omission he will spend the rest of the story paying for.

scenes.name: The stroke of midnight
scenes.summary: The first stroke of the clock reaches Cinderella mid-sentence. She runs before the twelfth, because the Fairy Godmother stated the condition plainly and Cinderella agreed to it.

scenes.name: The lost slipper
scenes.summary: On the palace stairs one glass slipper comes away and stays behind. It is the only thing the spell does not reclaim, and the only evidence the prince is left holding.

scenes.name: Back among the ashes
scenes.summary: Cinderella is at the hearth before dawn, in her own rags, the second slipper hidden. Her stepsisters come home full of the mysterious princess and describe her at length, to her face.

scenes.name: The prince's search
scenes.summary: The prince has the slipper carried from house to house across the kingdom. The method is absurd and everyone involved knows it, and it works anyway, because there is only one foot it can belong to.

scenes.name: The stepsisters' turn
scenes.summary: Both stepsisters force their feet at the slipper while the stepmother keeps Cinderella out of the room. Neither of them fits, and neither of them concedes it.

scenes.name: The slipper fits
scenes.summary: Cinderella asks to try, and it fits. Then she takes the matching slipper out of her pocket, which ends the argument before her stepmother can begin it.

characters.name: Cinderella
characters.description: A kind and hard-working young woman, treated as a servant in the house that was her father's. She obeys because refusing has never once worked, not because she agrees.
characters.personality: Patient and good-natured despite years of mistreatment, never bitter toward her stepfamily.
characters.motivation: Wishes, quietly and without much hope, for a single night of joy at the royal ball.
characters.qualities: Graceful, hardworking, and kind even to the mice and small creatures around the house.
characters.weaknesses: So used to obeying that she nearly gives up on the ball entirely until the Fairy Godmother intervenes.
characters.biography: Once a beloved daughter, reduced to a servant in her own home after her father remarried a cold widow with two daughters of her own.
characters.plannedTimeline: Marries the Prince once the glass slipper proves her identity, and by some tellings, forgives her stepfamily.

characters.name: Stepmother
characters.description: A cold, calculating widow who openly favours her own daughters. She never forbids Cinderella anything outright; she arranges circumstances so the refusal is never hers to defend.
characters.personality: Proud, controlling, and openly dismissive of Cinderella.
characters.motivation: Wants only her own daughters to marry well, and sees Cinderella as competition to be kept down.
characters.qualities: Sharp and strategic in running the household to her daughters' advantage.
characters.weaknesses: Her favoritism is so blatant that it fools no one outside the family, least of all the reader.
characters.biography: A widow who remarried Cinderella's father and, after his death, ruled the household entirely for her own daughters' benefit.
characters.plannedTimeline: Left humiliated once the glass slipper reveals Cinderella's identity before the whole court.

characters.name: The Elder Stepsister
characters.description: Cinderella's stepsister, vain and clumsy, and the first to reach for anything her sister wants.
characters.personality: Vain and quick-tempered, easily jealous of anyone prettier.
characters.motivation: Desperate to catch the Prince's eye at the ball, whatever the cost to Cinderella.
characters.qualities: Confident enough to try on the glass slipper herself without a shred of doubt.
characters.weaknesses: Her vanity blinds her to how unkind she is, right up to the moment the slipper simply will not fit.
characters.biography: The elder of Cinderella's two stepsisters, raised to believe her own comfort matters more than anyone else's.
characters.plannedTimeline: Fails to fit the glass slipper, exposing the family's cruelty before the whole court.

characters.name: The Younger Stepsister
characters.description: The other stepsister, just as vain as the elder and quicker to say aloud what their mother only implies.
characters.personality: Vain in her own right, though slightly less cruel than her elder sister.
characters.motivation: Follows her sister and mother's lead in hoping to marry above her station.
characters.qualities: Sociable enough to be tolerated at court, if not admired.
characters.weaknesses: Never questions the family's treatment of Cinderella, even when it plainly troubles her conscience.
characters.biography: The younger of Cinderella's two stepsisters, shaped by the same household that favored her over her stepsister.
characters.plannedTimeline: Also fails to fit the glass slipper, sharing in her family's public humiliation.

characters.name: The Fairy Godmother
characters.description: A godmother who appears once, at the worst hour, and helps on terms stated in advance. She lends; she does not give.
characters.personality: Warm, practical, and a little mischievous with her magic.
characters.motivation: Wants Cinderella to have her one chance at the ball, however briefly.
characters.qualities: Resourceful - able to turn a pumpkin, mice, and rags into a carriage, horses, and a gown in moments.
characters.weaknesses: Her magic is powerful but strictly timed, and cannot be extended past midnight.
characters.biography: A fairy who appears just as Cinderella gives up hope, transforming ordinary household things into everything she needs for one magical night.
characters.plannedTimeline: Vanishes from the story once her magic has done its work, never seen again after the ball.

characters.name: The Prince
characters.title: Heir to the throne
characters.description: The kingdom's heir, required to choose a bride at a single ball. He dances all night with a woman whose name he never thinks to ask for.
characters.personality: Attentive and sincere, taken with Cinderella's company rather than just her appearance.
characters.motivation: Wants to find the mysterious young woman who fled the ball, not just any bride.
characters.qualities: Persistent - determined to search the whole kingdom with the glass slipper until he finds her.
characters.weaknesses: Never even learns Cinderella's name at the ball, and nearly loses her for good when she flees.
characters.biography: The kingdom's heir, who dances all night with an unknown guest at his own ball and cannot forget her afterward.
characters.plannedTimeline: Finds Cinderella again through the glass slipper and marries her.

locations.name: The Kingdom
locations.description: The small kingdom Cinderella has never left, where the prince's family reigns and where a royal invitation reaches every house that has a door.
locations.climate: A cold hearth for Cinderella, who sleeps near the cinders for warmth while her stepfamily keeps the good rooms.
locations.culture: A household split in two - comfort and favor for the stepsisters, chores and silence for Cinderella.
locations.politics: Ruled entirely by the Stepmother, with no one to appeal to on Cinderella's behalf.

locations.name: Cinderella's House
locations.description: The house Cinderella's father left her, run since his death by her stepmother, who has never had to justify a single decision made inside it.
locations.climate: Brightly lit and festive for the ball, its grand staircase the setting for Cinderella's hurried midnight escape.
locations.culture: A court gathering meant to present every eligible young woman in the kingdom to the Prince.
locations.politics: The seat of the kingdom's royal family.

locations.name: The Kitchen Hearth
locations.description: The corner beside the kitchen fire where Cinderella sleeps. The ashes that settle on her there are where her name comes from, and the household uses it without thinking.

locations.name: The Garden
locations.description: The kitchen garden behind the house, with its pumpkin patch and its mice. Ordinary in every way until the night someone needs it to be otherwise.

locations.name: The Royal Palace
locations.description: Where the great ball is held, and where the prince is expected to choose a bride in one evening from a crowd of women he has never met.

worldRules.title: The Midnight Spell
worldRules.description: The Fairy Godmother's spell ends at the twelfth stroke of midnight, and everything it transformed returns to what it was. The hour is not a punishment or a test - it is stated up front, and Cinderella accepts it before anything is conjured.

worldRules.title: The Fairy Godmother's Transformations
worldRules.description: A wave of the wand turns a pumpkin into a carriage, mice into horses, a rat into a coachman and rags into a gown. Each transformation needs something real to work on: the magic changes what is there and never creates from nothing.

worldRules.title: What the Spell Cannot Undo
worldRules.description: The one exception to the rule above. The glass slippers were conjured rather than transformed, so midnight has no earlier state to return them to. A slipper lost on the stairs is still glass at dawn - and still the only proof that Cinderella was ever there.

notes.title: Continuity: the second slipper
notes.body: Cinderella has the matching slipper from the moment she gets home. Every scene after the ball has to be written as if she knows she can end the story whenever she chooses - and does not, until someone finally asks her.

notes.title: Visual motif: ashes and glass
notes.body: The two materials of the story. She is named for one and identified by the other. The hearth scenes and the palace scenes should keep trading them back and forth.

notes.title: Revision goal: nobody forbids her
notes.body: The stepmother never says no. She arranges circumstances instead, so that the obstacle is always a fact rather than a decision. Keep every obstacle in the first chapter deniable.

items.name: The Glass Slippers
items.description: A pair of slippers made of glass, conjured out of nothing rather than transformed from something. That is why they survive midnight when the rest of the spell does not.

items.name: The Pumpkin Carriage
items.description: A carriage made from a garden pumpkin, drawn by horses that were mice an hour ago and driven by a coachman who was a rat. Borrowed, in every sense.

items.name: The Ball Gown
items.description: A gown conjured from Cinderella's own rags, which is why it goes back to being rags: the spell only lends what it borrowed.

itemJourneys.newState: A pumpkin again, on the road
